subject: maths
title: Angles at a point and vertically opposite angles

scenes.heading: Angles at a point and opposite angles
scenes.sub: Find missing angles without a protractor
scenes.say: What if you could find an angle without measuring it at all? When lines meet or cross, the angles follow simple rules. Let's learn them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: All the slices of a pizza make the whole pizza
scenes.science: Angles at a point add to 360°; half the pizza is 180°
scenes.breaks: pizza slices are usually equal, but angles in a diagram can be any sizes. Only the total is fixed.
scenes.say: Think of a pizza. However you slice it, the slices add back up to the whole pizza. That's three hundred and sixty degrees. Cut it in half with a straight cut and each half is one hundred and eighty. But unlike most pizzas, the angles don't have to be equal. Only the total is fixed.
scenes.caption: However you slice a pizza, the slices add up to the whole: 360°. Cut it in half with a straight cut and each half is 180°. The angles don't have to be equal. Only the total is fixed.

scenes.heading: The angle rules
points: At a point: angles add to 360°
Lines cross: opposite angles are equal
scenes.say: Here are the rules. Angles on a straight line add to one hundred and eighty degrees. Angles that fill a right angle add to ninety. Angles all the way round a point add to three hundred and sixty. And when two lines cross, the vertically opposite angles are equal.
scenes.caption: Angles on a straight line add to 180°. Angles that fill a right angle add to 90°. Angles round a point add to 360°. When two lines cross, vertically opposite angles are equal.

scenes.heading: Two words to keep apart
scenes.say: Two words to keep apart. Complementary angles add to ninety degrees: C for corner. Supplementary angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees: S for straight.

scenes.heading: Angles at a point
scenes.question: Four angles meet at a point: 140°, 95°, 70° and c°. Find c.
lines: Angles at a point add to 360°
scenes.say: Four angles meet at a point: one forty, ninety-five, seventy and c. Angles at a point add to three sixty. The known ones add to three hundred and five. So c is three sixty minus three oh five, which is fifty-five.
scenes.caption: Four angles meet at a point: 140°, 95°, 70° and c°. They add to 360°. The known ones add to 305. So c = 360 − 305 = 55.

scenes.heading: Two lines cross
scenes.question: Two straight lines cross. One angle is 62°. Find the other three.
scenes.say: Two lines cross and one angle is sixty-two degrees. The opposite angle is also sixty-two. The angle next to it is on a straight line, so it's one eighty minus sixty-two, which is one hundred and eighteen. And the one opposite that is one hundred and eighteen too.
scenes.caption: Two lines cross and one angle is 62°. The opposite angle is also 62°. The angle next to it is 180 − 62 = 118°. The one opposite that is 118° too.

points: Always write the rule as your reason
scenes.say: Quick recap. Straight line, one eighty. Right angle, ninety. Around a point, three sixty. Vertically opposite angles are equal. And always write the rule as your reason. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Straight line, 180°. Right angle, 90°. Around a point, 360°. Vertically opposite angles are equal. Always write the rule as your reason. Now try the practice questions!
